title: Shut it down or double down: the story of Kit (ConvertKit)
disclosure: AFFILIATE LINK IN DESCRIPTION - AI VOICE

scenes.narration: October 2014. After almost two years of work, a small email tool makes about thirteen hundred dollars a month. A friend says: shut it down, or double down.

title: SHUT IT DOWN
OR DOUBLE DOWN?
scenes.subtitle: THE STORY OF KIT
scenes.narration: This is the story of ConvertKit, the email tool that is now called Kit, and the one choice that saved it.

scenes.label: HOME OFFICE
scenes.narration: Rewind to 2012. Nathan Barry is a designer who writes and sells his own ebooks online. Email is how he sells them.

scenes.label: SIDE PROJECT
scenes.narration: In 2013 he starts a side project, in public, on his blog: a simple email tool for creators like him. He calls it ConvertKit.

scenes.label: PART-TIME
scenes.narration: But growth is slow. He still sells books and only works on the tool part-time. Months pass, and the numbers barely move.

scenes.label: CONVERTKIT
scenes.narration: By late 2014, monthly revenue has slipped to about thirteen hundred dollars. That is not a salary. It is barely a hobby.
Most founders would quietly close it. Nathan asks himself one question: is the idea bad, or did I never really try?

scenes.label: DECISION
scenes.narration: He doubles down. He closes his other business, hires a full-time developer, and puts in about fifty thousand dollars of his own money.

scenes.label: SALES DESK
scenes.narration: Then the key move. Instead of selling to everyone, he picks one group: professional bloggers. And he reaches out to them directly.

scenes.label: MIGRATION TEAM
scenes.narration: He also removes their biggest fear. His team moves their email lists over for them, for free. Switching suddenly feels easy.

scenes.label: SERVER ROOM
scenes.narration: It works. Monthly revenue jumps from about three thousand dollars in January 2015 to about ninety-seven thousand by December.

scenes.label: NEW NAME
scenes.narration: In 2018, success brings a big mistake. The company renames itself Seva. But seva is a sacred word for many Sikh and Hindu people.

scenes.label: CEO SUITE
scenes.narration: Nathan listens to the community, says publicly that they got it wrong, and changes the name back to ConvertKit within weeks.

scenes.label: REBRAND
scenes.narration: In 2024 they try again, the right way. They talk to customers first, buy the domain kit dot com, and become Kit.
Today Kit is still self-funded. Outside estimates put its yearly revenue at roughly fifty million dollars.

scenes.label: TODAY
scenes.narration: From thirteen hundred dollars a month to tens of millions a year, because one founder chose to double down.
